pages.title: Client capabilities (caps): model, issue/revoke, flush, max_size, snapflush, release

features.name: Cap bit model (p, As/Ax, Ls/Lx, Xs/Xx, Fs/Fx/Fc/Fr/Fw/Fb/Fa/Fl) and cap strings
features.description: Generic cap bits (s,x,c,r,w,b,a,l) shifted per lock (auth 2, link 4, xattr 6, file 8); PIN bit 0; composite masks ANY_SHARED/ANY_RD/ANY_EXCL/ANY_FILE_WR/ANY_WR; DIR_CREATE=Fc and DIR_UNLINK=Fr on directories; getattr masks CEPH_STAT_CAP_*.
features.notes: Bit values are a hard wire contract. Fa (GWREXTEND) is never granted by any lock state.

features.name: File mode to wanted caps
features.description: ceph_flags_to_mode maps O_* flags to PIN/RD/WR/RDWR/LAZY; ceph_caps_for_mode gives wanted caps (RD: Fs Fr Fc, WR: Fx Fw Fb As Ax Xs Xx, LAZY: Fl, always p).
features.notes: Kernel and libcephfs compute the same mapping client-side.

features.name: Lock-state-derived allowed caps (any / loner / xlocker / replica)
features.description: Each state of filelock and simplelock (auth/link/xattr) defines caps for any client, extra for the loner, extra for the xlocking client and for replicas; get_allowed_caps composes them per client and masks by quarantine, quiesce, dir-op and old-client feature rules.
features.notes: This is how cache coherency (POSIX read-after-write across clients) is enforced.

features.name: Loner (exclusive client) selection
features.description: Picks a single non-stale client wanting write/read (files) or holding a cap on a non-delegation-point dir as loner; loner-mode lock states (EXCL) give it exclusive caps; dropping the loner requires its caps to fit the non-loner view.
features.notes: Performance mechanism (enables write-back caching); disabled when any replica MDS wants caps.

features.name: Wanted-cap-driven lock state transitions
features.description: file_eval/simple_eval choose EXCL/MIX/SYNC/LOCK from loner/other wanted caps and lock usage; transitions gather (revoke) conflicting caps.
features.notes: Determines whether clients do buffered/cached or synchronous I/O.

features.name: Cap issue in request replies
features.description: encode_inodestat creates a cap for the requester if needed and issues (wanted|liked)&allowed without revoking, sets last_issue, encodes ceph_mds_reply_cap with AUTH flag, max_size=min(committed,projected), inline data and xattrs if newer; snapshot inodes get the CAP_ANY view of the lock states (code comment: read-only) without a Capability, with cap_id/wanted left unset.
features.notes: No caps issued when session stale, inode frozen, exporting caps, or readdir crosses a snaprealm.

features.name: New caps on open/create/mknod/mkdir
features.description: issue_new_caps creates a cap (marked new) or ORs the file mode's caps into an existing cap's wanted, suppressing cap messages while re-evaluating locks; new-inode caps get cap_id 1; openc presets authlock/xattrlock EXCL and (write mode) a [0, stripe_unit] client range; mknod (regular file) and mkdir preset filelock/authlock/xattrlock EXCL and reset wanted to 0, mknod also sets the stripe_unit range.
features.notes: kclient async create assumes cap_id 1 and max_size = stripe_unit.

features.name: GRANT/REVOKE cap messages with seq/issue_seq/mseq tracking
features.description: issue_caps sends GRANT when only adding bits and REVOKE when removing; per-cap last_sent seq, last_issue, mseq; revoke history (_revokes) lets stale acks be interpreted; stale-session and invalid-cap special cases. seq bookkeeping per op: replies, GRANT/REVOKE and max_size GRANTs bump last_sent; TRUNC reuses it; FLUSH_ACK echoes the client's seq; EXPORT carries seq 0; IMPORT carries last_sent with issue_seq == seq.

features.name: Revocation gather on lock transitions
features.description: Lock transitions call issued_caps_need_gather and issue_caps; eval_gather completes the transition only when issued (not just pending) caps fit the target state.
features.notes: Client round trip is on the critical path of conflicting operations.

features.name: Client cap update / ack processing
features.description: handle_client_caps validates session/rank state, inode, cap, cap_id, mseq and freeze state, confirms receipt, infers null snapflushes, adjusts wanted, applies dirty metadata and re-evaluates locks; UPDATE/FLUSH/DROP/RELEASE/RENEW ops are treated alike.

features.name: Dirty metadata flush with FLUSH_ACK after journaling
features.description: Dirty bits Fw/Fx/Ax/Xx carry size, mtime, atime, ctime, time_warp_seq, change_attr, mode/uid/gid/btime, xattrs, inline data, fscrypt fields; applied with monotonic rules in an EUpdate('cap update') with forced wrlocks; FLUSH_ACK sent from the journal-safe callback.
features.notes: No MDSAuthCaps permission check on flushed metadata; caller_uid/gid ignored; the dirty mask is not checked against the bits the cap holds (Locker.cc:3391, :3645-3668). atime is applied only with dirty Fx (Locker.cc:4033), although kclient dirties Fw for a forward atime change.

features.name: Flush idempotency (completed_flushes, oldest_flush_tid)
features.description: Acked flush tids are remembered per session (persisted in session_info_t and journaled as metablob client_flushes); re-sent flushes are acked without reapplying; oldest_flush_tid trims; warnings and MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID when not advancing.
features.notes: Needed for exactly-once metadata flush semantics across MDS failover.

features.name: Synchronous flush (CEPH_CLIENT_CAPS_SYNC) and log-flush heuristics
features.description: FLAG_SYNC forces an MDLog flush; otherwise flush only if wanted caps are blocked by locked unstable locks, dirty locks have waiters, or max_size grew; otherwise the ack waits for the periodic tick flush (5 s), another explicit flush, or the Journaler flushing a completed journal object.
features.notes: fsync latency depends on it.

features.name: Wanted caps tracking with issue_seq rule
features.description: adjust_cap_wanted replaces wanted only when issue_seq == last_issue, otherwise only adds bits; propagates to auth via MInodeFileCaps on replicas; logs EOpen and prioritizes recovery.

features.name: max_size / client_ranges (journaled writeable ranges)
features.description: Per-client writeable byte range in inode_t.client_ranges, grown by doubling (capped by mds_client_writeable_range_max_inc_objs objects, rounded to layout period), journaled before being shared (clients see min(committed, projected)); explicit client requests via max_size; GRANT pushes new max_size.
features.notes: Bounds file size recovery after client/MDS failure; kclient blocks writes past max_size.

features.name: File size recovery after client loss
features.description: When a client with a writeable range loses its caps (stale revoke, kill, missing reconnect) the inode is marked NEEDSRECOVER; the next filelock transition probes objects up to max_size and journals the recovered size.

features.name: Truncate notification (CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC)
features.description: After a shrinking truncate is journaled, every cap holder receives TRUNC with truncate_seq/truncate_size/size; then max_size is re-checked.

features.name: Snapflush (FLUSHSNAP / FLUSHSNAP_ACK, null snapflush, nudges)
features.description: On COW after a snapshot, clients with WR caps must flush snapshot metadata; snapped inode locks held in SNAP_SYNC until then; MDS infers null snapflushes from releases without FLAG_PENDING_CAPSNAP; caps_tick nudges by kicking head locks after mds_freeze_tree_timeout/3.
features.notes: Snapshots are not POSIX but required for CephFS snapshot consistency.

features.name: Batched cap release (MClientCapRelease)
features.description: Clients release caps in batches (kclient: one page, about 170 items) with osd_epoch_barrier; MDS removes caps unless cap_id/mseq mismatch or the cap was re-issued after the release (issue_seq < last_issue).

features.name: Cap releases embedded in requests
features.description: ceph_mds_request_release items in MClientRequest drop caps/dentry leases before processing; suppressed eval; kick_cap_releases re-issues at request cleanup if nothing was sent since.
features.notes: Avoids revoke round trips for unlink/rename/setattr etc.

features.name: Stale session cap handling
features.description: Session cap_gen bump invalidates caps; non-WR revocations are forced, WR revocations cause eviction (blocklist per mds_session_blocklist_on_timeout); stale caps ignored for loner/wanted; resume re-evaluates locks and re-issues caps to the now-invalid caps as GRANTs (only notable caps for LAZY_CAP_WANTED clients).

features.name: Late revoke detection, warnings, health and eviction
features.description: revoking_caps lists ordered by revoke time; caps_tick clog warnings with exponential backoff; MDS_CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE(_MANY) health via beacon; optional eviction after mds_cap_revoke_eviction_timeout.

features.name: Replica caps and MInodeFileCaps wanted propagation
features.description: Replicas issue only replica-column caps and forward the union of their clients' wanted caps to the auth (mds_caps_wanted), which disables loner mode.

features.name: Cap export/import to clients (EXPORT/IMPORT ops)
features.description: Subtree migration, cross-rank rename and rejoin move caps between ranks; exporter sends EXPORT with peer {cap_id, issue_seq, mseq, mds, flags}; importer sends IMPORT with snap trace and peer, mseq increased; FLAG_RELEASE asks client to release the peer cap; EXPORT with mds=-1 drops caps. Caps created by a subtree import are marked STATE_IMPORTING until import_finish so import_reverse can drop them.
features.notes: Detailed in subtree-migration page.

features.name: Replica cap gathering (MGatherCaps, MExportCaps/Ack)
features.description: Auth asks replicas to ship their client caps (e.g. for quota broadcast); replica exports caps to auth which imports them and notifies clients.

features.name: OSD epoch barrier propagation
features.description: Every cap message carries osd_epoch_barrier; clients must have that OSD map before using caps; client-reported barriers in caps/releases raise the MDS barrier.
features.notes: Makes eviction/blocklisting safe before others get write caps.

features.name: Quarantine cap masking and EQUARANTINED errno
features.description: Inodes under quarantine allow only p to sessions without quarantine access; grants/revokes carry oserrno=-EQUARANTINED.
features.notes: kclient 7.3 does not decode MClientCaps v14 oserrno.

features.name: Quiesce cap masking
features.description: While an inode is quiesced, allowed/wanted caps are masked to ANY_RD|Fc|Fb|p, revoking write/exclusive caps.

features.name: Directory-op caps via lock caches (DIR_CREATE / DIR_UNLINK)
features.description: Fc/Fr on directories are granted only through MDLockCache for CREATE/UNLINK when the client holds Fx; revoked on lock-cache invalidation.
features.notes: Detailed in leases-lock-caches-and-async-dirops page.

features.name: Feature-gated cap restrictions for old clients
features.description: Caps record NOINLINE/NOPOOLNS/NOQUOTA from connection features; Fr/Fw withheld for inline-data or pool-namespace files from clients lacking support; quota pushes skipped.

features.name: Xattr blob and inline data piggybacking on caps
features.description: Xattr blob shipped in grants/replies when Xs pending and version newer than client_xattr_version; inline data likewise; xattr flush limited by mdsmap max_xattr_size (oversize ignored but version bumped).

features.name: subvolume_id in cap acks
features.description: FLUSH_ACK and FLUSHSNAP_ACK carry the inode's subvolume id (MClientCaps v13) for client-side subvolume metrics.
features.notes: Not set on GRANT/REVOKE/IMPORT.

features.name: Session message counting for cap messages
features.description: Every MClientCaps (and lease/snap/quota) message increments Session::cap_push_seq; REQUEST_CLOSE must carry the matching seq.

features.name: Cap reconnect after MDS failover
features.description: Reconnect recreates caps (issue_norevoke, seq reset), records dirty caps of early re-sent flushes, chooses lock states from issued|dirty, re-issues all caps on active, rebuilds snapflush expectations.
features.notes: Detailed in resolve-and-rejoin page.

features.name: OpenFileTable tracking of inodes with notable caps
features.description: Inodes whose caps want Fr/Fw/any WR or are client-writeable are added to the OpenFileTable (and EOpen logged) so they can be prefetched after failover.

features.name: Lazy I/O cap (Fl)
features.description: Fl granted in SYNC/MIX states only when wanted (O_LAZY); never 'liked'.
features.notes: Relaxes POSIX coherency by design.

features.name: Readdir cap acquisition throttle
features.description: Readdir requests are delayed when a session holds more than mds_max_caps_per_client*1.1 caps and its cap acquisition rate exceeds mds_session_cap_acquisition_throttle.

features.name: Cap-backed NFS delegations (Ganesha via libcephfs)
features.description: libcephfs read/write delegations require p As Ls Xs Fs Fr Fc (+ Fx Fw Fb for write) and are recalled when the MDS revokes those caps.
features.notes: MDS-side behavior is ordinary revocation.

features.name: Cap observability (perf counters, admin dumps)
features.description: Counters mds.caps, inodes_with_caps, mds_mem.cap/cap+/cap-, handle_client_caps(_dirty), handle_client_cap_release, process_request_cap_release, ceph_cap_op_* and cap_revoke_eviction; dump inode shows client_caps/loner; session ls shows num_caps.
features.notes: mgr status/dashboard read mds_mem.cap.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock around all cap processing
serialization_points.shared_state: all cap, lock, session and journal-callback state
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single big lock protects every cache object; cap messages, journal completions and ticks all take it.
serialization_points.notes: True conflicts are per (inode, client) cap state and per session bookkeeping.

serialization_points.name: Per-cap state machine (issue/confirm_receipt)
serialization_points.why_serialized: Seq-ordered protocol: interpretation of an ack depends on all messages sent before it.
serialization_points.notes: Scope is (inode, client); messages for one cap must be processed and sent in order.

serialization_points.name: Revocation gather blocks lock transitions
serialization_points.shared_state: lock state vs. issued caps of all clients on the inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: A lock cannot reach a state whose allowed caps exclude bits clients may still be using.
serialization_points.notes: Requires a client round trip; must not block a thread.

serialization_points.name: Forced wrlocks during cap-flush journaling
serialization_points.why_serialized: Prevents readers/lock transitions from observing pre-commit metadata until the EUpdate is safe.
serialization_points.notes: Only conflicts with operations that read or transition those locks on the same inode.

serialization_points.name: Single MDLog and journal-ordered FLUSH_ACKs
serialization_points.why_serialized: All cap updates of a rank go through one journal; acks fire from the safe callback in submission order.
serialization_points.notes: Clients only need per-inode tid order and durability before ack.

serialization_points.name: max_size growth needs filelock wrlock and journal commit
serialization_points.why_serialized: The writeable range must be durable before the client may write beyond the old max_size; may require a filelock state change.

serialization_points.name: Session completed_flushes and oldest_flush_tid trimming
serialization_points.why_serialized: Flush tids are client-global; dedupe and trimming must see one consistent set per session.
serialization_points.notes: Persisted in sessionmap and journal metablobs.

serialization_points.name: Session caps list ordering, cap_gen and push_seq
serialization_points.why_serialized: Every cap mutation may reorder the session list; every counted message increments push_seq.
serialization_points.notes: push_seq counting must match message delivery order (REQUEST_CLOSE).

serialization_points.name: Per-connection FIFO of cap messages
serialization_points.why_serialized: Seq numbers assigned under the lock must be delivered in the same order.

serialization_points.name: Global revoking_caps and per-client revoking lists
serialization_points.why_serialized: Late-revoke detection needs ordered revoke timestamps.

serialization_points.name: last_cap_id allocation
serialization_points.why_serialized: Rank-wide counter for new cap ids.
serialization_points.notes: Only per-(inode, client) uniqueness is needed.

serialization_points.name: SnapRealm cap lists
serialization_points.why_serialized: Realm membership for snap notifications and splits.

serialization_points.name: OpenFileTable updates on notable-cap changes
serialization_points.why_serialized: Tracks open/writeable inodes for recovery prefetch.

serialization_points.name: osd_epoch_barrier max tracking
serialization_points.why_serialized: Monotonic maximum stamped on every cap message.

serialization_points.name: Freeze deferral of cap messages
serialization_points.why_serialized: Cap state must not change while an inode is being exported.

serialization_points.name: Stale processing across a session's caps
serialization_points.shared_state: all notable caps of one session
serialization_points.why_serialized: Decide eviction (any WR being revoked) and force-revoke others.

serialization_points.name: Replica wanted caps disable loner
serialization_points.why_serialized: Exclusive client caps cannot coexist with replica-issued caps.

serialization_points.name: Pending snapflush auth pins
serialization_points.shared_state: head and snapped inode auth pins, SNAP_SYNC locks
serialization_points.why_serialized: Snapped metadata unreadable until client flushes; blocks freezing.

external_contract.detail: p=1, As=4, Ax=8, Ls=16, Lx=32, Xs=64, Xx=128, Fs=0x100, Fx=0x200, Fc=0x400, Fr=0x800, Fw=0x1000, Fb=0x2000, Fa=0x4000, Fl=0x8000; DIR_CREATE=Fc, DIR_UNLINK=Fr on directories.

CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_CAPS 0x310; ceph_mds_caps_head + body (EXPORT uses peer struct at body start), snap trace, xattrs in middle, versioned trailer up to v14; kclient sends v12 and decodes up to v12; ops GRANT 0 .. RENEW 12.
MDS uses REVOKE whenever bits are removed; kclient always responds to REVOKE with a cap UPDATE (after Fb writeback / Fc invalidation if needed).
seq increases for every GRANT/REVOKE/IMPORT/reply-issued cap on a given MDS connection; kclient treats seq <= cap->seq as a pre-IMPORT message and merges.

Client updates issue_seq only when a cap is added from a reply or IMPORT (and sets it to the message seq when releasing an unknown cap); echoes it in updates and releases. The MDS replaces wanted only when issue_seq == last_issue (otherwise only adds bits) and removes a cap on release only if issue_seq >= last_issue (otherwise just cleans old revoke records).
mseq increases on each auth migration; client picks the AUTH-flagged cap with highest mseq as auth cap; MDS drops messages/releases with older mseq.
Cap identity per (inode, client, MDS); stale cap_id updates/releases ignored; new-inode caps use cap_id 1 (kclient async create hard-codes 1).
Header tid = flush tid; cumulative per inode (all flushes with tid <= T cleaned); sent only after journal commit; must be in tid order per inode.
Client sends FLUSHSNAP with cap_id 0, seq 0, auth mseq, snap_follows, tid; MDS ack must echo snap_follows and tid.
CEPH_CLIENT_CAPS_SYNC forces MDS log flush (fsync); PENDING_CAPSNAP suppresses null-snapflush inference.

Client writes block beyond max_size; client requests bigger max_size via UPDATE max_size field or reports size; MDS grants via GRANT with max_size = min(committed, projected) range; accepted only from auth cap with file-write caps.
For async-created inodes the client assumes caps CEPH_CAP_ALL_FILE, cap_id 1, seq 0, max_size = layout stripe_unit; MDS openc presets authlock/xattrlock EXCL and client_ranges [0, stripe_unit].
Carries truncate_seq/truncate_size/size; client applies newer truncate_seq.

peer {cap_id, issue_seq, mseq, mds, flags}; EXPORT peer at size offset; IMPORT includes snap trace; FLAG_RELEASE releases peer cap; client re-sends pending flushes after IMPORT; EXPORT with mds=-1 drops the cap.

CEPH_SESSION_STALE makes the client bump s_cap_gen and treat caps as p only; MDS bumps Session::cap_gen; on RENEWCAPS resume_stale_caps re-evaluates, and issue_caps re-issues (wanted|liked)&allowed to the now-invalid caps as a GRANT (preceded by a GRANT re-issuing pending when bits must also be revoked).

CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_CAPRELEASE v2: num + {ino, cap_id, migrate_seq, issue_seq} items + osd_epoch_barrier; kclient batches about 170 items per page; it releases with the message seq as issue_seq when it gets GRANT/REVOKE/IMPORT for an unknown inode or GRANT/REVOKE for an inode without a cap from that MDS.
ceph_mds_request_release items (caps=implemented after drop, wanted, seq, issue_seq, mseq, dname lease) processed before the request.
Each cap/lease/snap/quota message increments client s_seq; REQUEST_CLOSE seq must equal MDS push_seq.
Caps carry osd_epoch_barrier; client waits for that OSD map before using caps; MDS adopts client-reported barriers.
Client resets seq/issue_seq/mseq to 0 and drops ANY_DIR_OPS bits in reconnect; may re-send flushes before reconnect when flushing caps were revoked.
subvolume_id (on FLUSH_ACK/FLUSHSNAP_ACK) feeds per-subvolume metrics; oserrno -EQUARANTINED marks quarantined inodes.
libcephfs delegations are backed by caps (RD: p As Ls Xs Fs Fr Fc; WR adds Fx Fw Fb); revoking them triggers delegation recall to NFS clients.
MDS_CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE(_MANY) for clients not answering revokes within session_timeout; MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID(_MANY) for clients not advancing oldest flush tid.
mgr status/dashboard read mds_mem.cap; session ls num_caps.

external_contract.item: Blocklist on eviction of write-cap holders
external_contract.detail: Clients holding write caps that cannot be revoked (stale) are evicted with OSD blocklist (mds_session_blocklist_on_timeout).

kclient adds every IMPORTed cap as AUTH (only the auth rank may send IMPORT); on EXPORT it creates a placeholder target cap with seq = issue_seq = peer.issue_seq - 1 and mseq = peer.mseq, so the IMPORT must carry seq == peer.issue_seq; with FLAG_AUTH it logs 'mismatched seq/mseq' unless IMPORT peer.issue_seq/peer.mseq equal the exporter cap's seq/mseq.
When truncate_seq increases (TRUNC or grant), kclient WARNs if it still holds Fr or Fl; the C++ MDS xlocks filelock for SETATTR(size) and O_TRUNC, whose xlock states allow only Fcb.

kclient dirties Fw (not Fx) when setattr only moves atime forward while holding Fw; the C++ MDS applies atime only when Fx is dirty, so that flush does not apply the new atime (inferred from code reading, not tested).

rust_implications.implication: Capability state is naturally owned by the inode's shard and keyed by (inode, client); all transitions for one cap must be serialized (seq protocol), but caps of different inodes, even for the same client, can be processed concurrently.

rust_implications.topic: Per-session ordering of outbound cap messages
rust_implications.implication: Seq assignment and enqueue to the client connection must be atomic with respect to other messages for the same cap, and the per-session outbound queue must be FIFO; when several shards send to one session, seq for a given cap must never be delivered out of order (assign seq inside the inode critical section and enqueue in that order).

Per-shard journals are compatible with the kernel contract as long as all cap-flush events of one inode go to one journal stream and acks are emitted after commit in per-inode tid order; no global order across inodes is required.

Flush tids are client-global while inodes live in different shards; the completed-flush set and oldest_flush_tid trimming must be either per (session, shard) with a client-global trim watermark or kept in a session-level structure that every shard journal can contribute to at replay (equivalent of EMetaBlob client_flushes).

Only per-(inode, client, rank) uniqueness across cap incarnations is required plus the fixed value 1 for caps created together with a new inode (kclient async create). A global counter is unnecessary; a per-shard or per-inode generation suffices, but ids must stay distinct from 1-based reuse after reconnect (raise to max reported).

Lock acquisition must treat outstanding client caps as a wait condition resolved by client messages (or session staleness), never blocking a worker thread; the hierarchical lock manager needs cap-aware state (allowed caps per mode for loner/other/xlocker) to decide what to revoke.

C++ recomputes quarantine access per issue by building the inode path string and looking up session auth caps; a shard should cache per-inode subvolume/quarantine membership and per-session access to make issue_caps O(clients) without path walks.

Each max_size extension is a journaled inode update (doubling growth, capped at 1024 objects by default) that must commit before the GRANT; for NFS/Ganesha sequential writers this is a frequent synchronous step and should use a fast per-shard journal path; max_size must never exceed the durable range.

In C++ dmClock only schedules MClientRequest; cap flushes and max_size requests bypass per-subvolume QoS. A per-subvolume SLA design must decide whether cap messages (and their journal writes) are rate limited, keeping in mind that delaying REVOKE acks or FLUSH_ACKs stalls other clients and fsync.

Marking a session stale must fan out to every shard holding its caps (bump cap generation, force-revoke non-WR revoking caps, detect WR revocations for eviction) and produce one session-level decision; maintain a per-session index of notable caps per shard to avoid scanning all caps.

The C++ MDS blocks lock transitions on an inode while a cap flush is uncommitted; an equivalent per-inode 'pending durable update' guard is needed so readers never observe uncommitted flushed metadata, but it only conflicts with the same inode.

Pending snapflushes pin snapped and head inodes and block freezing in C++; shard migration in Rust must either carry pending snapflush state with the inode or wait; nudging (revoking WR caps) after a timeout is needed to bound waits.

rust_implications.topic: Deferral instead of drop during shard moves
rust_implications.implication: C++ defers cap messages on frozen inodes and retries them in order; a Rust shard move must preserve per-inode ordering of queued client cap messages and request-embedded releases (same predicate) or clients can deadlock.

Inter-MDS encodings (Capability::Export/Import, MExportCaps) are free to redesign, but client-visible EXPORT/IMPORT messages (peer cap_id/issue_seq/mseq/mds/flags, mseq increase, snap trace on IMPORT, FLAG_RELEASE) are a hard contract if more than one active rank exists; within one rank, moving an inode between shards needs no client-visible message.
If the Rust design never replicates inodes to other ranks for client service, replica caps, MInodeFileCaps and MGatherCaps can be omitted; clients only need a single auth cap per inode.

C++ pre-grants all allowed caps except Fl (files) and file-data bits (dirs); clients rely only on getting at least what they need, so a Rust MDS may choose a different pre-grant policy, but must still answer wanted caps and must revoke with REVOKE ops.
Global revoking lists are only for health/eviction; per-shard lists aggregated by a periodic task are sufficient to produce MDS_CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE and the clog warnings with backoff.

C++ applies Ax/Xx flushed metadata without MDSAuthCaps checks (client-side enforcement); a Rust MDS must decide whether to keep this trust model (compatibility with kclient/libcephfs) or validate, without breaking root_squash expectations. The C++ MDS also does not check the dirty mask against issued caps; any such validation must allow flushes re-sent after a revocation ack, reconnect or IMPORT, when the MDS's issued view may already lack the dirty bits (confirm_receipt runs before _do_cap_update).
A rank-wide monotonic atomic epoch stamped on every cap message is sufficient; it must be raised on blocklisting and on client-reported barriers before any new caps are issued to other clients.
Every counted message (caps, leases, snaps, quota) sent by any shard must increment one per-session counter in send order; REQUEST_CLOSE validation depends on the exact count.

open_questions: Kernel snapshot (Linux 7.3-rc6) advertises CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS as feature bit 22 while the C++ MDS at this commit defines bit 22 as CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP (src/mds/cephfs_features.h:53); the impact on charmap/subvolume behavior is unverified and belongs to the wire-protocol/sessions pages.

Does any out-of-tree client still send flock state (flockbl) in cap UPDATE messages? The MDS inserts such locks in _do_cap_update (src/mds/Locker.cc:4161), but kclient always sends a zero-length blob (linux/fs/ceph/caps.c:1336) and in-tree libcephfs only sends file locks in reconnect (src/client/Client.cc:3486); other clients unverified.
Whether the Rust MDS should keep accepting client-flushed Ax/Xx metadata without MDSAuthCaps validation (C++ ignores caller_uid/gid in MClientCaps).
Seq comparisons in confirm_receipt and _do_cap_release are not wrap-aware; whether any client can wrap a 32-bit per-cap seq in practice is unverified.

FLUSH_ACK latency without CEPH_CLIENT_CAPS_SYNC: verified triggers are MDSRankDispatcher::tick (mdlog->flush every mds_tick_interval), explicit Locker/Server flushes, and Journaler::append_entry flushing when the write position crosses a journal object boundary (src/osdc/Journaler.cc:632-641); other Journaler/Objecter-level triggers are covered on the mdlog page, not here.

The MDS does not validate the dirty mask of a cap flush against the cap's issued bits (Locker.cc:3391, :3645-3668). Whether a Rust MDS should reject or mask such flushes (kclient never sends them) is a design decision; the C++ behaviour is inferred from code reading, not tested.
